issues.description: The type of the Developer.monthsOfSwiftExperience property is inconsistent across artifacts. The problem statement and the template declare monthsOfSwiftExperience as Int? (optional Int), but the solution implements it as Double?. This mismatch can confuse students about the expected type and lead to failing tests or type-related implementation errors when they follow the specification in the problem/template.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the type of monthsOfSwiftExperience consistent across all artifacts. Preferably change the solution to use Int? (optional Int) to match the problem statement and template: declare monthsOfSwiftExperience: Int? and update the initializer parameter and any related logic (e.g., arithmetic and switch) to operate on Int values. Alternatively, if Double is intended, update the problem statement and template to specify Double? and adjust examples accordingly.

issues.description: The concept 'monthsOfSwiftExperience' is described in the problem statement and declared in the template as an optional Int (Int?), but the solution repository uses an optional Double (Double?) for the same property and constructor parameter. This type divergence for the same conceptual attribute breaks a clear mapping between the problem description, the starter code and the reference solution and may confuse students about the expected type and how to implement the required logic (e.g., incrementing months, switching on value == 1).
issues.suggestedFix: Use the same type for monthsOfSwiftExperience across all artifacts. Update the solution repository to declare monthsOfSwiftExperience as Int? (and change the initializer parameter to Int?) so it matches the problem statement and the template. Adjust any arithmetic or switch logic in the solution accordingly (use Int arithmetic and compare against 1 as an Int).
